# g3d

> g3d is a Pure Go 3D rendering library, not a game engine: a scene graph of nodes with parent-child transforms, perspective and orthographic cameras, box, sphere, plane and custom buffer geometry, an unlit BasicMaterial and a StandardMaterial (metallic-roughness parameters, Blinn-Phong shading today), ambient and directional lights, and a forward renderer with frustum culling and render buckets. It draws through gogpu/wgpu, so the same code runs on Vulkan, Metal, DirectX 12, OpenGL ES and a CPU software backend. Zero CGO; Go 1.25+.
>
> Two ways in: `NewRenderer` takes a `gpucontext.DeviceProvider` (for example a gogpu app) and shares its device; `NewRendererFromDevice` takes a `*wgpu.Device` and queue directly. `Render` draws a scene into a texture view; `RenderTo` records into a command encoder the caller owns, for composing with gogpu/gg or gogpu/ui in one frame. Pre-1.0: the API may change before v1.0. Planned next: Cook-Torrance PBR, textures, shadows, then glTF 2.0.

- [API reference](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/gogpu/g3d): package documentation
- [README](https://github.com/gogpu/g3d/blob/main/README.md): overview, features, backends, integration, roadmap

## Examples

- [hello-cube](https://github.com/gogpu/g3d/tree/main/examples/hello-cube): rotating lit cube, the minimal g3d + gogpu program
- [fullscreen-overlay](https://github.com/gogpu/g3d/tree/main/examples/fullscreen-overlay): 3D scene with a 2D HUD drawn by gogpu/gg
- [viewport3d](https://github.com/gogpu/g3d/tree/main/examples/viewport3d): 3D viewport inside a gogpu/ui application
- [All examples](https://github.com/gogpu/g3d/tree/main/examples)
